# Copilot Instructions – Java Servlet-based Web Billing System
You are working in the repository [https://github.com/muneef-dev/hospital-management-system](https://github.com/muneef-dev/hospital-management-system). This project is a comprehensive hospital management system.
Now, I am building a web application using **Java Servlets** (layered architecture pattern), JSP, and MySQL, following the conventions and style of this repository.
When I ask you to implement a new feature (e.g., user registration), use: - Java Servlets for controllers - JSP for views - JDBC for database access - Follow the existing package structure and naming conventions in the repo - Use MySQL for database operations, with DAO and BO pattern - Organize code and files similarly to the current repo’s structure - Always include comments and explain any folder or file you create or modify - Make sure the code can integrate smoothly with existing functionality - Make sure to use CSS for views because this is a web application (the mentioned repo is not a web application)
For every new feature, provide: 1. Java Servlet code (controller) 2. JSP page(s) (view) 3. DAO and BO or database interaction code 4. SQL statements if new tables or changes are needed 5. Any configuration changes (web.xml, etc.) if needed 6. Add CSS files if needed
**Only use libraries already present in the repository unless told otherwise.**
---
## Project Goal Build a **Java Servlet-based web billing system** following layered architecture and the conventions of standard Java web apps.
## Architectural Requirements
- **Layered Architecture:** - **Presentation Layer:** Java Servlets and JSP files - **Business Logic Layer:** BO (Business Object) classes and DTOs - **Data Access Layer:** DAO (Data Access Object) classes and Entity classes
- **Design Patterns:** - Use Singleton, Factory, and Factory Method patterns as appropriate.
## Folder Structure
Follow this example structure:
``` src/ └── main/ └── java/ └── com/ └── example/ └── billingsystem/ ├── controller/ # Servlets and web controllers ├── bo/ # Business Objects and implementations │ ├── custom/ │ │ └── impl/ ├── dao/ # Data Access Objects and implementations │ ├── custom/ │ │ └── impl/ ├── dto/ # Data Transfer Objects ├── entity/ # Entity classes ├── util/ # Utility/helper classes └── ... # Other needed folders └── webapp/ ├── index.jsp # Entry point JSP ├── WEB-INF/ │ └── web.xml # Deployment descriptor ├── assets/ # Images, fonts, etc. ├── css/ # CSS ├── js/ # JS ├── view/ # Additional JSP files (optional, can be placed here or in root of webapp) └── ... # Other JSPs/static resources ```
## Implementation Guidelines
- **Servlets** go in `controller` package. - **JSP files** go in the `webapp` root (`index.jsp`) and optionally in `webapp/view/` for additional pages. - **Follow naming conventions** for BO, DAO, DTO, Entity as in the reference repo. - Implement billing operations (creating invoices, payments, displaying reports) using the layered architecture. - Use design patterns (Singleton, Factory) for BO/DAO instantiation.
## Database
- Use a relational database (e.g., MySQL). - Entities and DAOs should interact with the database using JDBC.
## Framework - Use **Tailwind CSS** for all styling. Link Tailwind CDN in the <head> tag. - Avoid any inline CSS — use only Tailwind utility classes.
## Design Principles 1. Simple and uncluttered layout — no unnecessary visual elements. 2. Minimalistic design with clean typography (use Tailwind's font-sans). 3. User-friendly navigation with a clear visual hierarchy. 4. Consistent spacing and alignment using Tailwind's spacing scale. 5. Fully responsive layout that adapts to mobile, tablet, and desktop.
## Additional Development Notes - use SuperBo.java, BoFactory.java in side bo package like in the reference repo. - use SuperDao.java, DaoFactory.java in side dao package also CrudDao, CrudUtil.java like in the reference repo. - use same code for DbConnection.java which is in the reference repo. - use same code/ code structure for entire project like in the reference repo. - use same codes if need in util package like in the reference repo. example - KeyGenerator.java, PasswordManager.java, etc. if needed
## Documentation
- Document major classes, responsibilities, and folder usage. - Provide sample servlet and JSP files for billing operations.
---
- **Document your code and decisions**: use Copilot to help write clear, concise documentation.
*Reference for architecture: Standard Java Servlet/JSP layered app and [`hospital-management-system`](https://github.com/muneef-dev/hospital-management-system)*

# Pahana Edu Bookshop - Version 1 Implementation Guide
## Project Overview
Create a web-based bookshop management system for Pahana Edu bookshop in Colombo City. The system should manage customer accounts, item inventory, and billing information.
## Core Requirements
Implement the following functionalities in Version 1:
1. **User Authentication (Login)** - Username/password authentication - Session management - Logout functionality
2. **Customer Management** - Add new customer accounts with: - Account number (unique) - Name - Address - Telephone number - Edit existing customer information - View customer details
3. **Item Management** - Add new items with: - Item code - Name - Description - Price - Stock quantity - Update existing item information - Delete items - List all items
4. **Billing System** - Calculate bills based on items purchased - Generate printable receipts
5. **Help Section** - Basic usage guidelines - FAQ
6. **System Exit** - Logout functionality
## Technical Specifications
- **Backend**: Java Servlets - **Frontend**: JSP with Tailwind CSS - **Database**: MySQL - **Server**: Apache Tomcat - **Build Tool**: Maven
## Database Schema
Implement the following tables: - users (authentication) - customers (customer details) - items (inventory) - orders (customer purchases) - order_items (items in each order)
## Implementation Guidelines
### 1. DTO and Entity
Create the following DTO and Entity classes: - User (authentication) - Customer (customer details) - Item (inventory items) - Order (purchase order) - OrderItem (line items)
### 2. DAOs and BOs
Implement DAO and BO classes for nessary operations: - User - Customer - Item - Order
### 3. Controllers
Create servlet controllers for: - User (Authentication - login/logout) - Customer - Item - Order/billing - Help section
### 4. Views (JSP)
Design user interfaces for: - Login page - Dashboard - Customer management (add, edit, view) - Item management (add, edit, delete, list) - Order/Billing creation - Receipt generation - Help page
### 5. Utilities
Implement utility classes for: - Input validation - Session management
## UI Design Guidelines
- Use Tailwind CSS for responsive design - Create a clean, intuitive interface - Implement form validation - Display appropriate error messages - Use consistent styling throughout the application
## Security Requirements
- Secure password storage - Input validation to prevent SQL injection - Session management - CSRF protection
## Development Process
1. Set up project structure and dependencies 2. Create database schema 3. Implement core DTO, Entities,BOs and DAOs 4. Develop authentication system 5. Create customer management features 6. Implement item management 7. Develop order/billing system 8. Add help section 9. Implement UI with Tailwind CSS 10. Test functionality
## Testing Guidelines - for now don't test because I will do it later
- Test form validations - Test CRUD operations - Verify calculations in billing - Test with different screen sizes for responsive design
